ok after some investigations (heavily assisted by Claude) I think here's where things stand
there are actually two issues going on here (and I think both errors are windows exclusive):

1. enableArtifactCache was enabled with Physlib#1582. lean4#12203 hard links cache artifact, which makes the files read-only.
  • On Linux and macOS, replacing a file by renaming another over it doesn't care about the old file's read-only permission or its hard links. It only needs write permission on the folder, and Lake's cache copy is left untouched. So they're almost certainly not affected.
  • On Windows, that final rename is the step that fails with os error 5 when the old file is a read-only hard link.

this may be of interest to @Mac Malone and @Kim Morrison as well

Claude's suggested upstream fix

Three possible fixes, from most to least targeted:

  1. Make leantar handle it (my recommendation). leantar ships with the Lean toolchain (since 2026-03), so this is effectively a Lean-side fix, although its code lives in digama0/leangz. On Windows, its final rename should work when the target is a read-only hard link. Windows has a rename option for exactly this: FILE_RENAME_FLAG_IGNORE_READONLY_ATTRIBUTE, available since Windows 10 (1809). Alternatively it could delete the old target before renaming, but on Windows that means clearing the read-only flag first, and the flag is shared with Lake's cache copy. That would silently remove the cache entry's protection, so the rename option is cleaner. It keeps all of #12203's benefits and changes nothing on Linux or macOS. I haven't tested it.
  2. Let a project opt a dependency out of the inherited artifact cache. Since #12034, enableArtifactCache also applies to Mathlib, even though Mathlib manages its own files through cache get. A per-dependency opt-out would stop Mathlib's files becoming read-only links. This needs a new Lake setting, and it only avoids the conflict rather than fixing it.
  3. An option to copy instead of hard link (for example on Windows only). The simplest to implement, but it gives up #12203's disk and speed savings for everything.

a workaround would be to first delete the outdated olean files. Physlib#1688 was supposed to implement that, which brings me to the next issue

1. Windows does not come with a pre-installed native C compiler.

C compiler is needed because of leansqlite and UnicodeBasic which was used in doc-gen4. if Physlib users practically never build docs locally, I suggest we removing doc-gen4 from Physlib's dependency list

Claude's response

Two separate things are going on:

1. doc-gen4 isn't covered by lake exe cache get. Mathlib's cache only contains Mathlib and its own dependencies (Batteries, Aesop, Qq and so on). doc-gen4 is a dependency of Physlib only, so nothing downloads it prebuilt. Whenever something needs it, Lake compiles it on your machine. Two of its dependencies, leansqlite and UnicodeBasic, contain C code, and Lake compiles that with the system C compiler (cc), which most Windows machines don't have.

2. Only building a Physlib program needs that C code.

Command Needs doc-gen4's C code? On Windows without cc
lake exe cache get (Mathlib's program) No works
lake build (Physlib's libraries) No: Physlib's code doesn't import doc-gen4 works
lake exe get_cache, linters (Physlib's programs) Yes: Lake links the C libraries of Physlib's whole dependency tree into every Physlib program fails

That's why cache get has never caused problems. get_cache, though, fails to build ("failed to execute 'cc'") before any of its code runs, so the stale-file cleanup from #1688 never happens. This only started affecting users when #1582 made get_cache the README's setup step.

I tested both directions on Windows. With no cc on the PATH, building get_cache fails on leansqlite and UnicodeBasic. With the doc-gen4 requirement removed from the lakefile, it builds and runs. The suggested fix is to move doc-gen4 into a separate docs project, as Batteries does with docs/lakefile.toml.
I agree on the vscode server part, in future version bump instructions we can add an extra step to restart vscode before building

Ok so I think we need to do three things then:

  1. Remove 
[[require]]
name = "«doc-gen4»"
git = "https://github.com/leanprover/doc-gen4"
rev = "v4.34.0"

from the toml file.

  1. Add a script which adds this back into the toml file at the right place, with a 'rev' matching that of Mathlib.
  2. Update the workflow on the website so that it runs that script before building.
